text:
alex: Heads-up — I ran a 24h perf sweep on pool-130 (dedicated) after the kernel-selector change. Noticed short, repeatable token-latency spikes that line up with KV-cache eviction bursts. Posting quick notes + query snippets so we can decide dashboard panels/alerts.

jen: Can you TL;DR the impact? p95/p99 numbers and how often?

alex: TL;DR: baseline p95 token latency ~12ms, during events p95 jumped to 80–120ms for ~30–90s windows, p99 hit ~250ms. Events ~6x in 24h, unrelated to request rate (stable). CPU/GPU %util looked normal. Kernel switched to fused-mha_v2 around the start of each window. KV cache evictions spike right before latency climbs.

sam: ugh. Do you have the raw metrics or a PromQL view we can paste into a dashboard?

alex: Yep — pasted the useful bits below. These are the queries I used (tested in grafana):
```promql
sum by(pool) (rate(inference_tokens_total[1m]))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by(le, pool) (rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])))
increase(kv_cache_evictions_total{pool="pool-130"}[10m])
(sum by(pool, kernel) (rate(kernel_selector_switch_total[5m])))
(sum by(pool) (rate(kv_cache_insert_total[5m])) / max(1, sum by(pool) (gpunode_cores_allocated)))
```

alex: Also captured a small timeline snippet from the trace logs:
```
[2026-01-12T14:02:47Z] selector: choose fused-mha_v2 for model/xyz seq=512
[2026-01-12T14:02:50Z] kvcache: evict 124 entries pool=pool-130 shard=3 reason=LRU
[2026-01-12T14:02:50Z] runtime: kernel_launch_time +42ms vs baseline
[2026-01-12T14:03:12Z] request: p95 token latency 94ms route=chat-completion
```

kevin: Suggest adding these panels to the dedicated-capacity dashboard for pool operators: per-pool token-latency breakdown (queue_ms | kernel_exec_ms | kv_lookup_ms | io_ms), kernel-selection timeline (stacked area with kernel names), kv-eviction heatmap (shard x hour), per-route p95/p99 overlaid with evictions, and a noisy-neighbor score panel.

maria: What's your definition of noisy-neighbor score? We should standardize it before alerting.

sam: Proposal: noisy_neighbor_score = normalize(evictions_per_core, 0..1) * 0.6 + normalize(p95_latency_jump,0..1) * 0.4. Trigger when score > 0.65 for 10m. We can refine weights later.

alex: I like that. For alerts, I'd add a suppression if kernel_selector_switch rate > X (we don't want false positives during planned kernel churn). Also include annotation for rollout windows.

kevin: For headroom panel: show allocatable throughput vs observed throughput, and compute headroom_pct = (alloc_throughput - observed_p95_throughput) / alloc_throughput. Color red < 20%.

jen: Can we get a quick prototype panel config? I can wire it into the dedicated-capacity dashboard if someone gives JSON/queries.

alex: I'll drop a minimal grafana JSON and a dashboard patch tonight. Quick sample alert rule (pseudo):
```yaml
alert: NoisyNeighborPool130
expr: (increase(kv_cache_evictions_total{pool="pool-130"}[5m]) / max(1, sum(gpunode_cores_allocated{pool="pool-130"}))) > 0.4 and histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by(le, pool) (rate(token_latency_bucket[5m]))) > 0.05
for: 10m
annotations:
  runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/noisy-neighbor
```

alex: (note the numbers are placeholders — we'll tune with offline data).

sam: Also instrument and export selector decision reason and fallback path counts. Right now we only see kernel name switches but not why the selector changed (quantization/seqlen heuristics). Add labels: selector_reason="seqlen_thresh" or "quant_profile".

maria: Agree. Also add a small perf counter for kernel warm-up penalty (time from first launch to steady throughput) — we've seen warmed vs cold kernel differences.

kevin: One more idea: show per-route fractional hit-rate on KV cache vs avg token-latency. Might reveal routes that suffer more from misses (rerank vs chat).

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout for runtime/kernel-selector v3.4 deployed to pool-120..pool-135 at 2026-01-12T13:50Z :rocket:

jen: ok, next steps: alex + sam to produce dashboard JSON + example queries. kevin to draft alert rules and headroom math. maria to spec new selector labels. I'll create a tracking ticket and assign owners.

alex: I'll upload the grafana json by EOD and link the ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:
